Definition: from G2827; a couch (for sleep, sickness, sitting or eating):--bed, table.
KeyPassages: Matthew 9:2; Matthew 9:6; Mark 4:21; Mark 7:4; Luke 5:18; Revelation 2:22
BiblicalUsage: Kline is a bed, a couch for sleep, sickness, or eating. Matthew 9:2 has the palsied man lying on a bed, and Matthew 9:6 has Jesus telling him to arise, take up his bed, and go to his house, Mark 4:21 asks whether a candle is brought to be put under a bed, Mark 7:4 counts the washing of tables among the traditions, Luke 5:18 has men bringing a palsied man in a bed to lay before Jesus, and Revelation 2:22 warns that Jezebel shall be cast into a bed of tribulation.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe a sickbed is where faith is proved: the palsied man was carried to Jesus on one, and told to carry it home on his own legs. I hold that the bed of sickness and the bed of tribulation are not the same bed, because the first is where Jesus heals and the second is where He judges.
